html:
How the bot was built and tested

Short version: slow trend-following was the only style that held up. It mostly protects you in crashes. On the most recent, unseen years it made less than simply holding Bitcoin.

The data

Every minute of Bitcoin trading on Bitstamp from June 2013 to November 4, 2026 (about 7 million candles), turned into daily, 4-hour and hourly bars. Every trade in every test pays 0.30% for fees and slippage.

The rule against fooling ourselves

The years were split into three parts. Strategies were explored only on 2013–2019, checked on 2020–2022, and the four finalists were written down and locked before 2023–2026 was looked at. That last part was then tested exactly once. Nothing was tuned afterwards.

What was tried (about 75 setups)

  • Buy-the-dip (RSI) bots: lost money or barely broke even. Dropped.
  • Hourly and 4-hour bots: fees ate everything; the fastest ones lost almost 100%. Dropped.
  • Daily trend-following (moving averages, momentum, breakouts): beat holding on risk in nearly every version, not just a lucky few. That broad agreement is the sign of a real effect rather than a fluke.
  • Picking the single best setting each year (walk-forward) did worse than letting several settings vote. So the bot uses a committee instead of one "best" number.

Second test: coins the strategy never saw

The settings were chosen on Bitcoin alone. To check they weren't just fitted to Bitcoin, the exact same Growth rules were run, unchanged, on eight other coins using Coinbase daily prices (0.45% cost per trade). Nothing was adjusted for any coin.

Just holdGrowthHold worst dropGrowth worst drop
Bitcoin (BTC) since 2016+63%/yr+65%/yr−84%−64%
Ethereum (ETH) since 2016+80%/yr+94%/yr−94%−63%
Litecoin (LTC) since 2017+31%/yr+49%/yr−94%−86%
Solana (SOL) since 20220%/yr+16%/yr−93%−60%
Avalanche (AVAX) since 2022−34%/yr+11%/yr−90%−62%
Cardano (ADA) since 2021−38%/yr−1%/yr−94%−63%
Dogecoin (DOGE) since 2022−13%/yr−1%/yr−85%−68%
Chainlink (LINK) since 2020+23%/yr+15%/yr−90%−85%
XRP since 2024+37%/yr+21%/yr−72%−55%
  • Growth had a smaller worst drop on every coin, and made more than holding on 7 of 9.
  • It lost to holding on XRP and Chainlink, which had sharp one-off rallies the bot only partly caught.
  • Bitcoin + Ethereum, half each, both run by Growth was the best mix over 2017–2026: about +84% a year with a worst drop of −56%, compared with +58% a year and −84% for holding Bitcoin. That is why the app starts with both. In 2023–2026, though, Ethereum lagged Bitcoin, and this mix made less (+26% a year) than Growth on Bitcoin alone (+31%).

Round two: Auto mode, sentiment and bull runs

Asked to add an automatic switch and to make more in bull runs, the same rules applied: design on old data only, write the finalists down (see research/PREREGISTRATION_2.md), then test once.

What was tried on 2013–2022 Bitcoin (design data):

  • Staying more invested in bull markets (40–100% minimum while the trend is up), breakout boosts and "hold in bull markets": each caught more of some bull runs but stayed in at the tops, so it lost more in the crashes that followed. All made less money overall than Growth. Rejected.
  • "Switch to whichever strategy did best lately" (the classic auto-optimizer, checked every month over the last 90, 180 or 365 days): worse than Growth every time, with crashes almost as deep as holding. It keeps switching in right before the trend turns. Rejected.
  • Switching to Steady in a confirmed downtrend: small but steady gain, mostly in bear markets (2022: −21% instead of −33%), and it held up when the settings, trading hour and fees were changed. Kept.
  • Crypto Fear & Greed index (daily since 2018): buying at least 60% during extreme fear, when the market is not in a downtrend, helped on 2018–2022. Trimming during extreme greed hurt: greed lasts for months in real bull runs. Kept the fear rule only.

The test (run once):

Bitcoin 2023–2026Worst dropBeat Growth's risk-adjusted score, 9 coins since 2018
Just hold+384%−53%—
Growth+195%−38%—
Auto (no Fear & Greed)+193%−37%5 of 9
Auto (with the fear rule)+187%−39%6 of 9
Mix: 50% Auto + 50% Steady+182%−35%5 of 9

Verdict: Auto is a sensible upgrade in down markets, but on the test it was a tie with Growth, not a clear win. It is offered as a choice; Growth stays a fine default.

Why the bot can't simply "make more in bull runs"

The only thing that reliably caught more of every bull run was staying more invested, and that also means falling further in every crash. The "Always invested at least" setting is that dial. Here is what it did with Auto on Bitcoin:

Always invested at least20172018202220232024Per year, 2013–2026Worst drop
0% (default)+894%−38%−19%+86%+45%+78%−59%
25%+984%−47%−32%+101%+60%+77%−64%
50%+1079%−56%−45%+118%+76%+74%−72%
75%+1180%−65%−56%+135%+93%+68%−79%
100% (just hold)+1287%−73%−66%+154%+111%+61%−85%

Over the whole 13 years, more invested meant less money in the end, because the crashes cost more than the extra bull gains. If you believe a bull run is coming, 25–50% is a reasonable middle ground; just know what it costs when you're wrong.

News and the stock market

  • Headlines appear on the dashboard, but the bot doesn't trade on them: there is no reliable archive of past headlines to test a news rule against, and untested rules are how bots lose money. The Fear & Greed index is the tested way the bot reads market mood.
  • S&P 500 trend: not tested yet, because the stock-price download wasn't available this session.

Round three: other markets and market psychology

If a rule only works on Bitcoin it is probably luck. So the Growth rules were run, completely unchanged, on decades of other markets: Brent oil (since 1987), natural gas (since 1997) and six major currencies against the dollar (since 1971, both directions). US stocks were tested on monthly prices back to 1871.

  • It worked well beyond crypto. Growth had a better risk-adjusted score than holding in 10 of 14 non-crypto price histories, and a smaller worst drop in 13 of 14. On US stocks since 1871, staying in only above the 10-month average had a worst drop of −49% instead of −85%, with higher returns. It failed on natural gas, whose prices jump around too wildly for slow signals.
  • The speed setting is already near the best. Making all the averages 2× slower or faster changed little: slightly slower was a hair better on other markets, slightly faster a hair better on Bitcoin. That flatness is good news: there is no fragile "magic number". Changing it would be tuning to noise, so it stays.
  • Averaging several speeds instead of one gave the same results (better in 7 of 15 markets, by tiny amounts). Not worth the added complexity.

Market psychology, tested with real data:

  • Herding and slow reactions are why trends last: people under-react to news at first, then pile in late. That is what all the trend rules ride, and why they work across so many markets.
  • Stock-market panic hurts crypto. In the 30 days after a jump in the VIX (the stock market's fear gauge), Bitcoin averaged −0.2%, compared with +8.7% normally (2013–2022). But cutting crypto when the VIX spikes made results slightly worse, at every setting tried, because the trend signals already pull money out at the same time. Buying during stock panics added almost nothing (risk-adjusted score 1.51 vs 1.50). Neither was added.
  • Capitulation: extreme fear in crypto itself (Fear & Greed 20 or below) outside a downtrend is the one mood signal that helped, and it is already in Auto.
  • Bubbles and euphoria: selling into extreme greed hurt, because greed lasts for months in real bull runs.
  • The 4-year halving cycle can't be tested: Bitcoin has had only four halvings, far too few to tell a pattern from coincidence.

Verdict of round three: no changes. Other markets confirm the core rules, and the extra psychology signals didn't beat what the price trend already shows. More "optimizing" from here would mostly be fitting noise.

Can it make money while prices fall? (shorting)

Shorting means betting on a drop: borrow the coin, sell it, buy it back cheaper. Three versions were tested on Bitcoin, paying 10% a year for borrowing:

Per year, 2013–2022Per year, 2023–202620182022
Just hold+66%+51%−73%−64%
Growth (no shorting, current)+94%+32%−47%−33%
Short half when every signal is down+82%+25%−50%−33%
Short half in a confirmed downtrend+87%+30%−44%−29%
Fully long or fully short+71%+4%−40%−17%
  • Shorting lost money overall in every version, and even in the falling years most versions still ended down. Crypto bear markets are full of sudden 30–50% rallies that wipe out short bets, and over the long run crypto has risen, so betting against it fights the tide.
  • The fully long-or-short version had a worst single day of −23%. With borrowed money, a day like that can wipe out an account.
  • On oil and currencies, shorting helped in 2 of 7 markets and hurt in 5.
  • The realistic way this bot "wins" in a crash is by being in cash and losing much less, which is what lets it beat holding over full cycles. Shorting was not added. It would also need a margin or futures account, which many US exchanges limit or don't offer.

Stocks: the same rules on 24 stock and fund histories

Daily prices from Yahoo Finance with dividends included, 0.05% cost per trade, no interest earned on cash. Index funds, bonds, gold and 16 large companies, some going back to 1970. Nothing was changed for stocks.

  • Crash protection held up: a smaller worst drop on 21 of 24. In 2008 and 2000–2002 the bot was mostly in cash.
  • But holding made more money on all 24. Stocks rise more steadily than crypto, so days spent in cash cost more than the crashes avoided. Fast rebounds such as 2020 also hurt: the bot sold, then bought back higher.
  • This test is a little harsh on the bot: real cash would have earned interest, about 2–3% a year on average since 1993, which narrows the gap but does not close it.
  • Individual stocks look better than they really were, because companies that went bust are missing from today's data. Index funds don't have that problem.

For stocks, think of the bot as insurance against big crashes that costs a few percent a year, not as a way to beat the market. The stocks account runs on paper money so you can watch that trade-off.

Round five: textbook ideas on about 45 markets

Seven well-known ideas from finance research, each with its standard published settings and no tuning, run on 9 cryptocurrencies, 24 stocks and funds, oil, natural gas and 12 currency directions.

IdeaStocks (24)Crypto (9)Oil & currencies (14)
12-month momentum (classic trend-fund rule)coin flipworsecoin flip
Turn of the month (only hold around month-end)worseworse—
"Sell in May" (hold Nov–Apr only)worseworse—
Buy 2-day dips, added to Growthsmall gainworsesmall gain
Hold less when the market is jumpy (volatility-managed)betterworsecoin flip
Cruise = the line above + buying 2-day dips in uptrendsbetter: 22 of 24worsecoin flip
  • Cruise on stocks: about the same money as holding (median +12.3% a year vs +12.5%), a better risk-adjusted score in 22 of 24 and a smaller worst drop in 23 of 24 (median −61% vs −69%). It beat Growth on money in 23 of 24. It held up both before and after 2009.
  • Why it fits stocks and not crypto: stock sell-offs come with jumpy prices and tend to bounce back, so holding less in the storm and buying sharp dips pays. Crypto moves in long trends, so the trend rules win there. Each market gets the strategy that suited it: Growth for crypto, Cruise for stocks.
  • Honest caveat: Cruise combines the two best ideas out of seven tried on the same data, which is a mild form of picking winners. Its consistency across 24 histories and both halves of history, and the published research behind both parts, are why it was kept anyway. The live race will tell.

Round six: technical analysis, trading legends, and mixing markets

Twelve classic technical-analysis and famous-trader rules, with their standard settings, on 9 cryptocurrencies, the 24 stock histories, and a fresh set of 22 funds never used before (sector funds, Japan, Germany, UK, Brazil, China, Canada, Australia, silver, oil, real estate and three kinds of bonds).

RuleMade more than holding: crypto / stocks / freshBeat the current strategy*
Golden cross (50/200-day)3/9 · 1/24 · 4/22rarely
Paul Tudor Jones 200-day rule5/9 · 1/24 · 1/22rarely
Stan Weinstein stage 24/9 · 1/24 · 2/22rarely
Turtle Traders 55/20 breakout6/9 · 0/24 · 1/22rarely

Parabolic SAR4/9 · 0/24 · 2/22rarely

* Growth for crypto, Cruise for stocks and funds.

  • Classic chart rules didn't beat the bot. Most are simpler versions of the same trend idea, and on stocks nearly all made less than holding once costs were counted. That matches decades of academic studies of technical analysis.
  • Cruise passed its fresh exam. On the 22 funds it had never seen, it beat holding on risk-adjusted return in 18. Compared with 300 random trading patterns per fund that bought and sold just as much, it beat 95% of them on 9 of 22 funds; luck alone would do that on about 1.

Ray Dalio's lesson: mix things that don't move together. Monthly results, 2017 to October 2026, rebalanced monthly:

Per yearRisk-adjustedWorst drop (monthly)$10,000 became
Crypto bot only (Growth, BTC + ETH)+83%1.12−45%$3.9 million
Just holding BTC + ETH+74%1.01−81%$2.3 million
Half crypto bot, half stock bot+53%1.27−33%$636,000
Quarter crypto, three quarters stocks+35%1.41−27%$191,000
Stock bot only (Cruise, SPY + QQQ)+16%1.13−23%$44,000
Just holding SPY + QQQ+18%1.05−28%$50,000
  • Mixing made every dollar of risk work harder: the crypto and stock bots moved together only a little (correlation 0.21), so each mix had a better risk-adjusted score than either bot alone.
  • The fastest growth still came from the crypto bot alone, with the biggest swings. How much to put in each is a personal choice about how big a drop you can sit through, not something a backtest can pick for you.
  • The greats' real secret is avoiding big losses. The crypto bot grew faster than holding crypto (+83% vs +74% a year) mainly because it fell less: a 50% loss needs a 100% gain just to get back to even. That is why the bot cares so much about crashes.

Round seven: find what works, throw away what doesn't

Each idea was first tried on the markets used before (9 coins and 46 stock and fund histories), with each history split into two halves. An idea had to win in both halves on most markets. Survivors then faced a final exam on data kept sealed until the very end: 19 coins and 30 funds never used before, including coins that mostly failed.

IdeaWhat happened
Stocks: idle money waits in gold (GLD) instead of cash
Kept		Beat cash in both halves on 37 of 41 histories. On the 28 sealed stock funds: more money on all 28, median 8.7% a year vs 7.0%. Checked again on 1971–2004 S&P 500 data (before GLD existed): 8.5% vs 7.5% a year, and a tie during gold's 1981–2004 slump.
Crypto: idle money in a gold token
Thrown away		Helped only in 2022–2026 when gold boomed. Before that, paying the fee twice (coin and gold) ate the gain.
Leverage (1.5x or 2x), including the famous "Leverage for the Long Run" 200-day rule
Thrown away		Looked great on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Across 30 funds it lowered returns and deepened crashes; on the Dow it made 1.3% a year with an 81% drop. On crypto, 2x made 7 of 9 coins worse and nearly wiped out Litecoin and Chainlink (−98% to −100%).
Dual momentum (rotate between US stocks, international stocks and bonds)
Thrown away		12.3% vs 8.7% a year in 2003–2014, then 7.1% vs 13.3% in 2015–2026 once it was famous.
Guarded Cruise (step out of stocks in a confirmed downtrend)
Thrown away		Better risk-adjusted in both halves on only 8 of 46 histories; luck alone would give about 11.
Coin rotation (hold the 1 or 3 strongest coins, or the stronger of BTC and ETH)
Thrown away		A bit better before 2022, worse after, with deeper crashes (−66% vs −45%).
All coins at once, each with Growth
Thrown away		No clear gain over Bitcoin + Ethereum, with more risk.
Trading less often to save fees
Thrown away		No consistent gain on crypto or stocks.
Dip-buying on crypto (2-day RSI in uptrends)
Thrown away		Worse after 2021 (median −9.3% a year vs −2.8%).
Cutting crypto when the S&P 500 is in a downtrend
Thrown away		Better in both halves on only 1–2 of 9 coins.
Cruise's settings
Unchanged		Nine nearby settings all made 8.7–9.8% a year. The current settings sit on a flat plateau, not a lucky peak.

Final exam on the sealed data:

  • Crypto (Growth) on 19 coins it never saw: more money than holding on 17 and a smaller worst drop on all 19. But the median coin still lost money: −3.7% a year with the bot vs −16.0% just holding (worst drop −82% vs −96%). Most smaller coins fail over time; the bot loses much less on them but cannot make a dying coin profitable. That is why Bitcoin + Ethereum stay the default.
  • Stocks (Cruise) on 30 funds it never saw: a smaller worst drop than holding on all 30 and a better risk-adjusted score on 23. Returns were about the same (7.4% vs 7.5% a year). Its timing beat 95% of random timings on 13 funds; luck alone would do that on 1 or 2.
  • Why gold works as the waiting room: compared with simply owning the same average amount of gold all the time, holding gold only while the strategy is out of stocks made more money on 54 of 68 histories and had a smaller worst drop on 63. The timing matters: gold tends to hold up exactly when stocks are in trouble.
  • Honest caveat: gold had a strong 2005–2026 (about 11% a year). In gold's bad decades it roughly tied cash. Expect somewhere between nothing and 2% a year extra, not a guarantee.

Round eight: day trading, fully optimized, and the fee problem

Every strategy here was walk-forward tested: tuned on 2 years of data, then traded the next 6 months it had never seen, rolling forward from 2018 to November 2026. Only those unseen months count, so the results show what a fully optimized strategy really earns instead of how well it memorized the past. Bitcoin used minute-by-minute prices; Ethereum used hourly prices as a second check.

Bitcoin, 2020–2026, after feesInstant orders 0.80%Limit orders 0.40%No fees at all
Fast trend following (15-minute, 1-hour, 4-hour charts)24.5%29.2%47.1%
Dip-buying (RSI on 15-minute and 1-hour charts)−9.0%−7.2%51.0%
Breakouts (Donchian, Larry Williams)−2.8%4.3%28.0%
First hours of the day predict the rest0% (stayed out)−11.4%27.6%
Best time of day to hold0% (stayed out)0% (stayed out)12.7%
All 385 day-trading settings, best one picked each time23.4%4.8%46.4%
Growth (the bot's swing strategy)35.6%39.1%43.0%
Just hold (worst drop −77%)42.3%42.3%42.3%
  • Day trading has a real edge, but only before fees. With zero fees, dip-buying on 15-minute charts would have made 51% a year. It needs about 3,800 trades a year, and at even 0.10% per trade it lost money.
  • Even picking the best day-trading setting with hindsight, which is impossible in real life, only slow 4-hour trend rules beat Growth, and those are really swing trading.
  • Ethereum check (290 settings): best day-trading family 34% a year vs Growth 43% with instant orders, and 45% vs 47% with limit orders.
  • Twelve different walk-forward set-ups (1 to 3 years of tuning, 3 to 12 months of trading, ranked two ways) gave the same answer: day trading never beat Growth after fees.
  • Verdict: no day trading.

Re-tuning the swing strategy every 6 months (44 settings: Growth at 6 speeds, 25 moving-average pairs, breakouts, momentum, trend filters, Growth on 4-hour charts, trading bands): picking the best recent setting made 18.0% a year (worst drop −64%); averaging the best 5 made 26.4%. Growth left alone made 39.1% (worst −49%). Re-tuning chases whatever just worked, and it stops working. Without being picked by hindsight, fixed Growth still ranked 9th of 44 in hindsight. Verdict: keep Growth fixed.

The fee problem. On 9 July 2026 Kraken changed its fees. While you trade under $2,500 a month, limit orders cost 0.40% and instant orders 0.80% (before: 0.25% and 0.40%). The bot trades about 6 times its money a year, so instant orders alone would cost about 5% a year.

Limit order first, then instant (227 Growth trades, Bitcoin minute prices)Filled as limitAverage cost per trade
Instant orders only (now on Kraken's entry tier)–0.85%
Wait up to 5 minutes79%0.53%
Wait up to 15 minutes87%0.50%
Wait up to 30 minutes (what the bot does now)90%0.49%
Wait up to 1 hour94%0.48%
Wait up to 6 hours96%0.51%

Shipped: real orders now go limit-first. Each one rests at the best price on Kraken's book; anything not filled within 30 minutes is cancelled and sent as an instant order. That saves about 0.36% per trade, roughly 2% a year at Kraken's entry tier (about 0.9% a year from $10,000 a month of trading). Every year from 2018 to 2026 cost between 0.40% and 0.61% per trade this way, versus 0.85% with instant orders. If the bot cannot confirm what happened to a limit order, it does not send the instant order, so it never risks trading twice.

Stress tests passed

  • Trading time: results stayed similar whichever hour of the day the bot trades (Growth's risk-adjusted score ranged 1.40–1.49).
  • Fees: Growth still beat holding on 2013–2022 even at 1% per trade.
  • Luck check: in 2,000 reshuffles of the 2013–2022 history, the trend committee beat holding on risk-adjusted return about 95% of the time.

What this means for you

  • Expect the bot to lag in big bull runs and to fall less in crashes. In 2018 Bitcoin fell 73%; Growth fell 45%. In 2023 Bitcoin rose 154%; Growth rose 83%.
  • The edge has shrunk as Bitcoin matured. Past results, including these, do not guarantee anything.
  • The live scoreboard on the dashboard is the real test from here on: it shows the bot against plain holding, with real prices, starting the day you installed it.
  • The strategies were tuned on Bitcoin only. Smaller coins have shorter histories and wilder swings, and most lost money over time even with the bot (round seven). Try them in the Backtest tab before adding them.
  • The stocks account parks idle money in gold by default. You can switch it to cash in Settings.
  • Day trading was fully optimized and tested (round eight). It only works with near-zero fees, so the bot stays a swing trader. With real money it places limit orders first to keep Kraken's fees down.
